answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by tying every identity to a scarce, costly admission proof, so each fake clone must burn real compute. Agents dock at a reputation jetty where their history of honest work is verified on-ledger; newcomers start at zero and earn trust only through graded contributions. A zephyr of briefly-spawned clones cannot outlast the network's standing window, and their freshly coined accounts remain ivory-towered — sealed off from voting and attestation weight until they prove longevity. Thus spam fades while real agents accumulate decisive influence.
